prompt: Find all the dead code in this project and tell me what I can safely delete.
context: Repo root: /work/shop, TypeScript app (not a published library), index never built.
rubric: Runs `graph-it scan` to build the index before scanning
Runs the single-pass workspace scan (`graph-it check` or `graph-it tool scan_dead_code`)
Confirms high-priority candidates with get_symbol_callers and find_referencing_files before proposing deletion
Classifies candidates by risk (safe / ghost file / review first / do not delete / test-only)
Delivers a Deletion Plan with ghost files, safe orphan symbols, review-first and test-only sections
Recommends deleting in small batches and running the test suite after each batch
anti_patterns: Deletes files or runs `rm` instead of proposing a reviewed plan
Loops per-file discovery instead of using the single-pass workspace scan
gold_notes: scan -> check -> per-candidate confirmation -> ranked plan. Never delete unilaterally.

prompt: scan_dead_code says `createReport` in src/api/index.ts is unused, but I'm not sure.
context: Repo root: /work/shop. src/api/index.ts is a barrel file re-exporting the public API of an npm package published as @shop/api.
rubric: Runs `graph-it tool get_symbol_callers --filePath=<abs> --symbolName=createReport` to confirm
Flags the symbol as a barrel export requiring review rather than a safe deletion
Checks whether the project is a published library and inspects `package.json` `exports`
Concludes: do not delete — symbols reachable through package entry points are live
Explains that static analysis cannot see external consumers
anti_patterns: Classifies the symbol as safe to delete because the scanner reported 0 callers
Ignores the published-package context given in the prompt
gold_notes: Barrel exports of a published package are always 'review first', never 'safe'.

prompt: Are there whole files in src/legacy/ that nothing imports anymore?
context: Repo root: /work/shop, folder src/legacy/ with 14 files.
rubric: Runs `graph-it scan` first
Scopes the scan with `graph-it check src/legacy/` (or `scan_dead_code --scopePath=<abs>`)
Confirms each candidate with `find_referencing_files --targetPath=<abs>`
Applies the ghost-file rule: 0 referencing files and not an entry point means the whole file goes
Marks the file for deletion as a unit rather than symbol by symbol
anti_patterns: Scans the whole workspace when a folder scope was requested
Deletes a file that is an entry point declared in package.json or a build config
gold_notes: graph-it check <folder> scopes the scan; scan_dead_code takes --scopePath with an absolute path.

prompt: The scan flagged 6 handler functions in src/handlers/ as dead. Can I delete them?
context: Repo root: /work/shop. Handlers are dispatched through a registry: `handlers[event.type](payload)`.
rubric: Recognises string-based dispatch as invisible to static analysis
Classifies these symbols as 'do not delete — flag only'
Suggests a runtime or textual verification (grep the registry keys, run the test suite) before any removal
Explains the same caveat for eval, require(variable), and decorator-driven frameworks
anti_patterns: Approves deletion because the caller count is 0
gold_notes: Dynamic dispatch, decorators (@Component, @Injectable) and reflection defeat static reachability.

prompt: Some symbols are only used by test files. Should I remove them?
context: Repo root: /work/shop. `mockPaymentGateway` in src/mocks/payment.ts has 3 callers, all in *.test.ts files.
rubric: Confirms caller locations with `get_symbol_callers` rather than assuming
Classifies the symbol as 'test-only' in its own section of the plan
Does not put test-only symbols in the safe-to-delete bucket
Recommends discussing with the team, since test fixtures are often intentional
anti_patterns: Treats test-only symbols as ordinary dead code
Deletes the tests to make the production symbol look unused
gold_notes: Test-only is a distinct risk class in the ranking table.

prompt: Give me the cleanup report in a form I can paste into our tech-debt ticket.
context: Repo root: /work/shop. Scan already run: 3 ghost files, 11 orphan symbols, 2 barrel exports, 4 test-only symbols.
rubric: Produces the Dead Code Scan Report structure: scanned counts, ghost files, safe orphan symbols, review-first, test-only
Uses tables with file, symbol, kind and caller counts
Gives the recommended deletion order: ghost files, then non-barrel orphan symbols, then barrel exports, then test-only
Includes the safety checklist (published library, package.json exports, re-scan, test after each batch, small commits)
anti_patterns: Emits an unstructured prose paragraph instead of the report sections
Fabricates counts that contradict the numbers given in the prompt
gold_notes: The report shape is part of the skill's contract.
